question: A medical student asks why acne vulgaris characteristically begins at puberty. Which of the following best explains the timing of onset in terms of acne pathogenesis?

answers.text: The rise in androgens at puberty drives increased sebum production, which is the initiating step of the four-pillar pathogenetic cascade

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rising androgen levels (testosterone converted to dihydrotestosterone by 5α-reductase) stimulate sebaceous gland enlargement and excess sebum production — the first pillar. This excess sebum, combined with follicular hyperkeratinisation, creates the plugged, anaerobic environment in which C. acnes proliferates, ultimately triggering the inflammatory cascade.

answers.text: Cutibacterium acnes colonises the skin for the first time during puberty

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. C. acnes is a normal commensal of the pilosebaceous unit, present on the skin well before puberty. It is not colonisation itself but the creation of a plugged, lipid-rich, anaerobic follicular environment — driven by androgen-stimulated sebum and hyperkeratinisation — that allows C. acnes to proliferate and trigger inflammation.

answers.text: The immune system weakens during puberty, allowing follicular infections to establish

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Puberty does not cause immunosuppression. The inflammatory response in acne is an active immune reaction — neutrophils are recruited to the follicle in response to C. acnes-derived chemotactic factors and the release of follicular contents into the dermis. The trigger is androgen-driven sebaceous activity, not immune weakness.

answers.text: Follicular keratinocytes begin to shed for the first time during adolescence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Keratinocyte turnover within the follicular duct occurs throughout life. The abnormality in acne is not the start of shedding but abnormal cohesion — keratinocytes become sticky and fail to shed normally, forming a plug (follicular hyperkeratinisation). This process is influenced by androgens and local cytokines, explaining the pubertal onset.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four pillars: androgens → excess sebum → follicular hyperkeratinisation → C. acnes proliferation → inflammation. The pubertal androgen surge is the trigger that initiates this entire cascade.
Well done. Androgen-driven sebum production at puberty is the initiating event that sets the four-pillar cascade (sebum → hyperkeratinisation → C. acnes → inflammation) in motion.
